commits.subject: Reconstruction v1.1.0: the cue lexicon is a hint, not a gate
commits.body:
Supersedes the "Auto-save: reconstruct.ts" commit, which carried this change
with no explanation.

THE BUG THIS FIXES IS A SILENT ONE. Until now the actionable pass only ran on
windows around sentences Layer 1's cue lexicon had already flagged:

    const actionable = candidates.filter(c => categoryOf(c.kind) === "actionable");
    const clusters = clusterByTime(actionable);   // Layer 2 only looked HERE

That made a 1,000-line Hinglish word list the hard recall ceiling on
assignments. A lecturer phrasing an obligation in words the list did not
contain produced no window, so the model was never pointed at that part of the
lecture -- and the assignment was invisible, with no error, no warning and no
empty state for anyone to notice. rules.ts records this happening twice: the
"research paper / case study / literature survey" terms and the entire
imperative lexicon were both added AFTER a real lecture came back empty.

Both passes now sweep the whole lecture. Cue hits are passed into each window
as evidence ABOUT that window instead of as permission to look at it -- which
is what the lexicon is genuinely good at. It is a cheap, precise, offline
prior, and a prior belongs in the prompt, not in the control flow. Where no cue
fired, the prompt says so and raises the bar for that window rather than
skipping it. Teaching already worked this way and needed no change.

Actionable windows OVERLAP by 60s (180s window, 120s stride). An obligation is
assembled from statements up to a minute apart -- four sentences over 45s in
the reference lecture -- so a boundary falling between the setup and the
pronoun referring back to it would destroy the exact case this layer exists
for. Verified: guaranteed co-read distance is 61s.

Overlap means one assignment can be reconstructed twice, so items are merged on
WHERE their evidence sits rather than on what they are called -- the model
words a title differently per window, but cites the same sentences, and those
are already verified character positions. Verified against six cases including
short-span-inside-long and zero-width spans.

COST, MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED. The sweep doubles the call count and lowers the
maximum lecture length this pipeline can handle on the request path:

    23 min   20 calls   ~200s   fits
    36 min   30 calls   ~300s   at the maxDuration limit
    50 min   42 calls   ~440s   TIMES OUT
    90 min   75 calls   ~760s   TIMES OUT

The ceiling drops from roughly 90 minutes to roughly 36. That is the price of
assignment recall and it is not fixable by tuning: reconstruction needs to move
off the request path into a background job. Concurrency is deliberately left at
4 -- the right value depends on the provider rate limit, which has not been
measured, and guessing it trades a known ceiling for silent 429 losses.

Version bumped to 1.1.0 so runs before and after remain comparable, per the
same contract extraction_method carries.

Verified: tsc clean, next build clean, eslint clean, overlap and dedupe
checked numerically.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Knowledge layer: reconstruct what a lecture MEANT, not which sentences looked interesting
commits.body:
Sentence-level extraction cannot represent a real assignment. In the reference
lecture one assignment spans four sentences over 45 seconds, and the fourth
("vo project ko cloud pe deploy karna hai") is only interpretable given the
third. A one-span extraction_candidates row cannot hold that shape, so the
product emitted two unrelated assignments instead of one.

Three layers now sit on top of the candidates. Candidates are NOT replaced:
they remain the immutable Layer-1 record and the baseline any future
extraction method is compared against.

  Layer 2, src/lib/reasoning -- reconstructs items from a bounded window around
  one candidate cluster. The model never sees the whole lecture, so it cannot
  pull in unrelated material or be steered by something said twenty minutes
  away. Every quote it returns is verified verbatim against that window, and an
  item with an unverifiable quote is DISCARDED rather than repaired -- which
  makes "never invent" a property of the pipeline instead of a line in a
  prompt. The schema requires an `unspecified` field, so a model asked what was
  NOT said has somewhere to put the gap rather than filling it.

  Layer 3, src/lib/knowledge -- stores the result. Knowledge is derived but not
  recomputed: it costs a model call to produce, it must stay citable months
  later, and a student asking the same question twice must get the same answer.

  Review moves from per-sentence to per-item. Only actionable kinds
  (assignment, deadline, exam_instruction) are gated behind a human; topics and
  concepts go live automatically. A professor cannot review thirty topics after
  every lecture, and the cost of being wrong is not symmetric -- a mislabelled
  topic wastes a moment, a wrong deadline costs a grade.

Schema: knowledge_items + knowledge_evidence, many spans per item, which is the
entire point of the second table. Already applied to the live Supabase project
(kkjyfojcahlopsfpcdbw), so this deploy does not need a migration step.

UI: CandidateReview is replaced by ActionableReview + KnowledgeUnit, and the
/api/lectures/[id]/taught route is superseded by /api/lectures/[id]/knowledge.
Adds npm run test:knowledge and test:identity.

Verified before pushing: next build clean across all 24 routes, eslint clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Lecture knowledge: extract what was TAUGHT, not only what was assigned
commits.body:
A real 23-minute college lecture on cloud computing produced exactly one
candidate: the deployment assignment in its final minute. The matcher was not
at fault and no tuning would have helped. Every value CandidateKind allowed --
assignment, deadline, exam_scope, announcement, guidance -- is a category of
ACTION, so there was no shape in the schema in which "the lecturer defined a
unified manager" could be stored even if something had detected it. Twenty-two
minutes of teaching had nowhere to go.

Same lecture now yields 32 items: 26 teaching, 5 actionable, 1 reference.

TEACHING EXTRACTION IS STRUCTURAL, NOT KEYWORD-BASED

src/lib/extraction/teaching.ts matches the six sentence shapes a lecturer uses
to signal teaching -- agenda, topic boundary, enumeration, naming, contrast,
Hinglish recap -- each with a capture group for the SUBJECT. A cloud-computing
word list would have scored well here and zero on a chemistry lecture; "the
next topic we have is" and "there are two types of" are the same in both. Those
shapes occur more than thirty times in this one transcript.

Composed with `rules` rather than merged into it, because the two have opposite
error costs: an obligation should be missed rather than invented, while a
teaching topic is cheap to over-produce and expensive to miss. Keeping them as
separate passes keeps those thresholds independently tunable. `rules` stays
registered unchanged as the actionable-only baseline.

THE ACTIONABLE HALF WAS ALSO WEAK, AND THAT WAS A GRAMMAR GAP

The assignment was set across five sentences and only the one containing
"karna hai" was caught. The lexicon was built entirely from the
infinitive-plus-auxiliary construction and was deaf to the imperative -- a
lecturer saying "questions likho, search karo, find out karo" is setting work
without ever using it. Added imperative mood, the addressed-deliverable case
("Assignment for you", which had scored 0.44 against a 0.45 floor because a
short-sentence penalty applied to a complete three-word sentence), and marks.

Worth recording: the first version of the imperative lexicon included the
infinitives karna/likhna/banana, and that immediately resurrected the exact
false positive the suppression rules exist to kill -- "derive karna hai" became
homework. The verb form IS the signal. Infinitives are now excluded by name.

"WHAT ALL WAS TAUGHT?"

New route /api/lectures/[id]/taught, answered from STORED knowledge and never
by re-reading the transcript -- a product that re-derives its answer from 22,000
characters on every question has no stored knowledge, only a summariser. The
answer is a structure, not prose: lesson scope, topics, concepts, breakdowns,
comparisons, assignments, references, each with the timestamp and the verbatim
sentence it came from. Faculty see unreviewed items badged `unconfirmed`;
students see only what a human has confirmed.

CONFIRM WAS NOT BROKEN UNDERNEATH

Reported as "0 pending · 1 ruled but the card is still there". The verdict was
written, the item became course knowledge, and a refresh preserved it -- the
queue simply rendered `[...pending, ...ruled]`, so nothing ever left it. A queue
whose items never leave is not a queue, and from outside "it worked" and "it did
nothing" looked identical. Ruled items now move to a collapsed section, and
pending is grouped by category. Teaching and references get a bulk confirm;
actionable deliberately does not, because a deadline must be read one at a time.

DELETE

Removes the audio, the row, and every candidate and verdict beneath it via the
existing cascades. Confirmation requires typing the lecture title, because a
dialog dismissed by reflex is not a confirmation and deleting the wrong lecture
is precisely the failure a reflexive click produces. Storage first, row second:
object removal is idempotent so a retry after a half-failure succeeds, while the
reverse order would strand audio nothing points at.

Also: the review queue and the summary now show only the MOST RECENT extraction
run rather than the newest version per method. Switching methods is now a real
event, and highest-version-per-method would have shown both sets at once.

VERIFIED ON THE REAL LECTURE, NOT A FIXTURE

Stored rows checked against a fresh in-memory extraction: same count, every
produced item stored, nothing in the database the extractor did not produce,
evidence text and confidence identical, all 32 char spans slicing back exactly,
every timestamp inside a real segment.

Browser-driven over CDP: 24 checks on the lecture page and 10 on deletion,
including that deleting a throwaway lecture in the same course leaves the real
one with all its rows, its audio and a working page.

lint 0, typecheck 0, build clean, extraction suite 76, provenance suite 16.

commits.subject: Verified on production: two recordings now produce two independent transcripts
commits.body:
Follow-up record for the lecture-identity fix. The diff landed under
729b180 Auto-save; this carries the reasoning and the verification results.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERION MET

scripts/verify-lecture-identity.mts, two 40-second clips cut from two different
lectures, run against https://copy-paste-labs.vercel.app with real Sarvam:
30 checks, 0 failures. Same suite against localhost: 30/30. Two different audio
files, two different runs, two different transcription results.

THE GUARD WAS TESTED, NOT ASSUMED

Built the production bundle, started it with VERCEL=1 and
TRANSCRIPTION_PROVIDER=fixture, and uploaded a file named to match a fixture
slug — the exact path that caused the original failure. Result: HTTP 500 with
"Replay would attach a transcript from a different recording to this lecture,
so it is refused", the lecture left at pending_upload, provider_job_id null,
raw_transcription_response null. No foreign transcript stored.

BLAST RADIUS

22 of 27 lectures carry a replayed transcript. 21 are this session's own test
uploads. Exactly one is a real user lecture: "Cloud computing"
(5ced44b6-e156-4ddb-9146-14035d366620), which extracted 21 candidates from a
thermodynamics transcript.

Zero of those candidates were confirmed, and zero students are enrolled in that
course. The confirmation gate did the job it exists for while the layer beneath
it was wrong: a bad transcript produced a bad review queue, not a false answer
to a student. That is not a defence of the bug — the transcript should never
have been foreign — but it is the difference between an embarrassment and a
retraction.

The row is left as it is. Re-transcribing overwrites a stored raw response, and
whether to do that is the operator's call, not a side effect of a bug fix.

A SEPARATE DEFECT FOUND BY MAKING THE FIRST LIVE CALL — NOT FIXED, BY INSTRUCTION

Clip B is an English DSP lecture. Sarvam returned romanized ARABIC for it on a
live call, with language_code sent explicitly as "en-IN". This is the 2026-08-21
Lab v0 failure reproducing, and it disproves the fix recorded for it: stating
the language does NOT prevent the misdetection.

Worse, all three guards stayed silent:

  language mismatch   the engine reported en-IN, matching what was sent
  low confidence      live batch responses carry NO language_probability at all
                      (it is null) — the heuristic only ever worked on the
                      captured fixtures, which have it
  transcript text     65 tokens, below the 120-token floor, so it refused to
                      judge

The text check would have caught it easily on merit: English function-word
ratio 0.015 against 0.427 for the genuine English clip in the same run. The
floor, not the signal, is what failed.

Reported rather than fixed: the instruction was to fix the identity pipeline
only and build nothing else.

commits.subject: Auto-save: verify-lecture-identity.mts, route.ts, build.ts +1 more (4 files)
Add public Privacy Policy and Terms of Service at /privacy and /terms
commits.body:
Google's OAuth consent screen requires both as public links on the app's own
domain, and it reviews them.

Written from what the code actually does rather than from a template. Where the
software has a gap, the document says so, because a policy describing a system
nobody built is worse than no policy — it is a promise that will be broken. The
three disclosures that a template would have missed:

  Retention.  This system is designed not to delete. Raw audio and the raw ASR
              response are preserved permanently and rejected extractions are
              retained, both deliberately — the evidence trail is the product,
              and it breaks if the source is thrown away. There is no automatic
              expiry of anything. That is unusual enough to need saying plainly.

  Children.   Classroom recordings carry the voices of students who may be under
              18. The DPDP Act 2023 requires verifiable parental consent for
              children's data, and this app implements no age verification and no
              consent mechanism. Stated as a "do not use with minors yet", not
              papered over.

  Consent.    Faculty upload recordings of other people. The app cannot obtain
              or verify that consent, so the terms put that obligation on the
              uploader explicitly rather than leaving it unowned.

The terms also state the thing students most need to hear: a confirmed item is
one faculty member's judgment about one sentence, not an official notice, and
the institution's own channels win where they disagree.

Both are linked from a footer on every page — an anonymous visitor must be able
to reach them, which is exactly what Google's review checks.

Neither document has been reviewed by a lawyer, and both say so at the top.
They close the "no consent/data-protection position" gap that progress.md has
carried as a blocker since 2026-07-29 only in the sense of being honest about
it; they do not make the app fit for real student data.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Deployed to Vercel: https://copy-paste-labs.vercel.app
commits.body:
Live and verified against production: 67 end-to-end checks and 33 language
checks, both green. That includes the full workflow — upload 10.5 MB of real
audio through a signed URL, transcribe, extract, confirm/edit/reject, then
re-enter as a student, ask a question and open the evidence — plus the negative
checks that matter, run against the deployed app rather than localhost.

THE PROJECT WAS ALREADY BROKEN AND LOOKED FINE

The existing Git integration had produced a Production deployment marked Ready
that served 404 on every path. Root Directory was unset, so Vercel found no
package.json at the repository root, detected no framework, built nothing in
2 seconds and deployed an empty site. Fixed Root Directory and the framework
preset via the API so Git pushes work, not just manual deploys.

A second thing worth writing down: `vercel --prod` from inside the app
directory fails on this project, and correctly so. The CLI uploads the current
directory as the deployment root and Vercel then applies Root Directory inside
that upload, so it looks for the path nested under itself. Deploy by pushing to
master, or run the CLI from the repository root.

THE SERVERLESS FIXES ALL HELD, IN THE REAL ENVIRONMENT

- Provenance written by a production function carries a real 40-character SHA
  from VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA, with no "commitHash could not be resolved"
  limitation. That branch would have degraded every record silently.
- The fixture provider ran inside a real serverless function, which is the only
  proof that outputFileTracingIncludes actually put the JSON in the bundle.
- The 28 MB upload path completed inside the 60s function ceiling.

REGION — MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED

This Supabase project resolves to 2406:da1a:… — AWS ap-south-1, Mumbai — and
Vercel had functions in iad1, Washington DC. Five calls to /api/courses, a
two-query endpoint:

  iad1   median 1545 ms   (1140-2328)
  bom1   median  389 ms   (151-1299, high end is a cold start)

Four times faster. Moved to bom1 and redeployed. The transcribe route moves a
whole audio object between Supabase and the provider, so this was not a
micro-optimisation.

ENV VARS

The Supabase integration had already wired the correct project — confirmed via
`vercel env pull`, because Vercel marks these sensitive and they can never be
read back through the API. Added SARVAM_API_KEY and TRANSCRIPTION_PROVIDER.

Everything is Production-only, so preview deployments have no Supabase config
and will fail at request time until the targets are widened. Noted in DEPLOY.md
rather than silently widened.

STILL TRUE AND STILL IMPORTANT: the deployment runs in replay mode. No live
Sarvam call has ever been made from this app. Every lecture uploaded right now
replays one of three captured transcripts, and says so in a visible panel.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Make ClassMind V1 deployable to Vercel, and add Google sign-in
commits.body:
Two requests, one commit, because the OAuth redirect URLs and the deployment
domain are the same problem.

VERCEL — three things would have failed in production only

1. `getCommitHash()` shelled out to `git`. Vercel builds ship with no .git
   directory and no git binary, so the execFileSync path always throws there and
   every provenance record would have carried "commitHash could not be
   resolved" — silently degrading the one field Constitution IV is strictest
   about. It now reads VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA first, which is necessarily clean
   because a deployment is built from a pushed commit.

2. The fixture provider reads its JSON with readdirSync. Nothing imports those
   files, so Next's dependency tracer could not see them and the serverless
   bundle would have shipped without them — ENOENT on the first transcribe, in
   production, with no local reproduction. `outputFileTracingIncludes` names
   them. Verified by grepping the built .nft.json trace: all three fixtures are
   in the transcribe function's bundle.

3. The transcribe route pulls a whole audio object out of Supabase Storage and
   pushes it to the provider — two large transfers in one request, and the only
   route in the app that is not milliseconds. It declares maxDuration = 60,
   which is the Hobby ceiling and accepted on every plan. A timeout is
   recoverable: the lecture stays pending_upload with its audio already stored.

Uploads were already safe — audio goes browser to Storage through a signed URL
and never touches a function, so Vercel's 4.5 MB request body limit does not
apply. That was a design decision made earlier for other reasons and it happens
to be what makes this deployable at all.

Verified the way that mattered: `next start` on the production build, with
`E2E_BASE_URL` pointed at it. 67 checks, 0 failures — the fixture provider
included, in production mode.

GOOGLE SIGN-IN

`/auth/callback` exchanges the code for a session on the cookie-bound client
(a fresh client would succeed and leave the user signed out), then creates a
profiles row ONLY if none exists — this route runs on every Google sign-in and
a blind upsert would overwrite a name or role the user had since changed.

Every failure path redirects to /signin?error= with a readable message: the
user is mid-navigation and there is no UI here to show an error in. `next` is
validated against open redirects — `//evil.com` and `/\evil.com` both start
with a slash and both leave the site, which is the textbook bug on this exact
endpoint. The redirect origin comes from x-forwarded-host so a proxied
deployment does not bounce users to an internal hostname.

The profile-creation path could not be exercised without a live provider, so it
was verified directly against the database instead: a fresh user has no profile
row, both roles insert, an invalid role is rejected by the check constraint, and
the row cascades away with the user.

DEPLOY.md and README.md carry the setup: Root Directory (the one setting that
breaks a naive deploy — this app is four levels down in a multi-project repo),
the environment variables, the Supabase redirect allow-list and why the wildcard
is mandatory, the Google Cloud Console redirect URI that people most often get
wrong, and function region — Vercel defaults to Washington DC and a Mumbai
Supabase project would put the Atlantic in the middle of a 50 MB transfer.

tsc 0, eslint 0, build clean across 20 routes. Suites: extraction 75,
provenance 16, e2e 67 (dev and prod builds), languages 33.

commits.subject: Auto-save: DEPLOY.md, next.config.ts, route.ts +2 more (5 files)
UI layer: fix 13 defects found by actually rendering it in a browser
commits.body:
The UI had never been opened. Typecheck, lint and build all passed on it, which
found none of the following. A parallel agent audited every component against
the API payloads it consumes, fixed what was wrong, and then drove real
headless Chrome over CDP with a genuine Supabase session, because the client
half cannot be verified any other way.

THE ONE THAT BROKE THE DEFINITION OF DONE

Processing never advanced outside the upload widget. LectureClient never polled
/poll and never offered /extract. Close the upload tab or reload the page and
the lecture sat at `transcribing` forever; a lecture that did reach
`transcribed` had no affordance anywhere in the UI to run extraction. The
backend was complete and correct the whole time — there was simply no way for a
faculty member to reach it after a refresh. Fixed with a LectureProgress
component that polls while in flight and offers recovery when stalled;
observed advancing untouched from "Transcribing · Queued" to "Published ·
21 candidates proposed for review" in 9 seconds.

THE REST

- Every plain lecture visit auto-sought and autoplayed, because
  `Number(searchParams.get("t") ?? "")` is `Number("")` is `0`, and
  `Number.isFinite(0)` is true.
- Evidence clicks off a segment boundary moved the audio and left the
  transcript still — the lookup matched exact segment starts only. Now snaps to
  the nearest segment.
- The deep-link jump re-fired on every refetch, restarting audio under the
  reader mid-poll.
- Extraction failure was reported as success: `.catch(() => undefined)`
  followed by "Done — candidates extracted".
- The middleware matcher had `"\."` inside a *string*, which collapses to `"."`
  — the extension test matched any character.
- `useSearchParams` had no Suspense boundary, which this Next version requires.
- Confirmed knowledge rendered as one flat list rather than grouped by kind.
- Ask results hid their supporting evidence behind a toggle, and the button
  submitted empty queries.
- Course-form errors were written into the course-list error slot, so they
  rendered at the top of the page and never cleared.

Left open deliberately: sign-up only persists the chosen role when Supabase
returns a session immediately, so with email confirmation on the role defaults
to faculty. Nothing in the UI branches on role — every surface branches on
isOwner — so this is inert until it isn't.

FINAL STATE

tsc 0, eslint 0, next build clean across 19 routes. Four suites, 191 checks,
all green: extraction 75, provenance 16, end-to-end 67, languages 33.

This commit is empty of diff for the UI files — autosave had already taken them
one at a time under `Auto-save: <component>.tsx`. It carries the reasoning,
which those 20-odd commits do not.

commits.subject: Session record for 2026-08-22 (empty commit: the content landed under Auto-save)
commits.body:
This commit adds no files. Everything it describes is already in the tree — the
autosave hook, firing on a subagent's file write, committed it as `02be8dc
Auto-save: candidates.json, evidence.json, session.md +1 more` before this
message could be attached to it. The charter asks for one intentional commit
per session whose message explains why, because for two of the three founders
the log IS the communication channel. So the message is recorded here even
though the diff is empty.

WHAT LANDED

ClassMind V1 stopped being code that compiled and became a workflow that runs.
Four suites, all green: extraction 75, provenance 16, end-to-end 67,
languages 33.

Running it for the first time found two defects, neither reachable by reading,
typechecking or building:

1. The extraction engine read an 18-minute university course-outline lecture as
   2 generic guidance items, missing the entire module-by-module syllabus and
   the prescribed textbook. Its lexicon had been built from a Class-12 coaching
   lecture. Two rules later: 21 candidates.

2. Worse: the provenance guard written for Lab v0's Arabic wrong-language
   failure could not see that failure. Sarvam had reported `language_code:
   "en-IN"` — the correct code — and only the transcript text was wrong. The
   guard compares reported against configured, so the branch was unreachable
   for the one input it existed for. Only the engine's 0.617 confidence caught
   it, clearing the 0.8 threshold by 0.183.

Both are the same mistake: code written against a description of a problem
rather than against the input that caused it.

DOCUMENTS

HANDOFF.md § 0 was actively dangerous — it still said nothing was committed and
HEAD was 53c39a6, false for two days. Rewritten; § 10 marked superseded rather
than edited; new § 11 covers how to run the product, the suites, the fixture
provider, the data model and the limitations.

decisions.md records the 2026-08-22 decision to build the Product Platform
before the walkthrough runs. It crosses the frozen protocol's stopping rule
completely, not on the technicality the 2026-08-11 entry could defend:
`extraction_candidates.kind` enumerates the domain model in a check constraint,
before the walkthrough meant to validate it. Cost stated rather than argued
away.

Inbox entry classmind/2026-08-22T0930Z-classmind-v1-build-and-verification,
4 candidates, 3 discarded for having a topic but no basis.

ALSO CARRIED HERE: the lecture route now returns only the newest extraction
version per method with a `supersededCount`, because bumping rules to 1.1.0
means a re-extracted lecture would otherwise show a reviewer the same sentence
twice. Its own commit was also lost to autosave, as `10deb6c Auto-save:
route.ts`.

32 of this session's 34 commits are `Auto-save:` messages naming one file while
containing others. That is captured as cand-004, and this empty commit is the
workaround, not the fix.
